documents: Visa, PR confirmation or PR card (new residents)
Proof you lived abroad 12+ months (returning Canadians)
Itemised list in English or French, values in Canadian dollars
BSF186 personal effects form, plus BSF186A list
Any papers stamped by border officers when you arrived
Liquor import declaration, if bringing alcohol
Arrival notice from your Canadian moving company
dutyFree: New residents: goods you owned and used before arriving in Canada
Returning residents: goods owned and used 6+ months, after 12+ months away
Antiques over 100 years old and art in a genuine household move
restricted: Cars must meet Canadian standards; used foreign vehicles are often not allowed
Alcohol is taxed, rules vary by province, and extra amounts need a permit
Firearms must be declared and usually need a licence; check before shipping
Plants, soil and meat are banned or tightly controlled; avoid shipping food
New, never-used items may be charged duty; keep receipts
notes: You must report to border officers on arrival and declare goods to follow
Get your BSF186 stamped at entry, or you may pay duty and tax
List any later shipments now so they can also come in duty free
Any single item worth over CAD 10,000 is taxed on the amount above that

documents: For a car: make, model, year and VIN
restricted: Vehicles need a B-13 export declaration filed by your mover
Car fuel must be at 1/8 tank or less when loaded
Vehicles must meet the destination country's import rules
notes: No export customs declaration is needed for household goods
